tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

I should load the dsh-semantic-ui skill and use DecisionExplorer probably. This is a tradeoff/decision question — DecisionExplorer fits. Let me load skill first.

<skill_resources>
Resources for this skill are managed by provider "runtime".
Load referenced resources only as needed.
</skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>
For relationships, tradeoffs, or numeric data, use dsh_semantic_ui only when exploration improves understanding. Choose ArchitectureExplorer, DecisionExplorer, or DataChart. Simple facts and short explanations need plain text. Use the unique dsh_semantic_ui tool with action=describe to obtain the selected component schema, then action=render with one versioned view. Keep only a conclusion and necessary explanation in prose. Never output UI specs or JSON/JSONL fences in the answer. Do not invent facts, values, evidence, rankings, or statistical methods. This applies equally to prose, summaries, node details and comparison cells. Distinguish supplied facts from conditional inferences; leave unspecified conditions unknown. Possible future needs are not settled plans. Known values do not outrank unknown values. Zero is an observed value with scale-specific meaning; replacing missing values with zero may bias results in either direction. Controls perform local deterministic changes, not new model analysis.

The only delivery entry is dsh_semantic_ui. Get the chosen component fields with action=describe, then deliver action=render. Display IDs are turn-scoped; revisions increase for updates. All schema and semantics are enforced at runtime.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>

The task: two storage options: A max 100GB, simple deployment; B max 1000GB, complex maintenance. Current need 80GB, future maybe 300GB. How to choose under different requirements?

This is a tradeoff decision → DecisionExplorer seems apt. Let me describe both DecisionExplorer and maybe DataChart.

Key facts: A capacity 100GB, simple deploy. B capacity 1000GB, complex maintenance. Current need 80GB; future possible 300GB. Unknowns: cost, maintenance burden details, growth timing/probability, performance, migration cost, whether A can be expanded beyond 100GB (no — cap 100), etc.

Decision logic:
- If need stays ≤100GB: A fits (80GB with 20GB headroom = 20%; that's tight, no room to grow).
- If need reaches 300GB: A impossible (exceeds 100GB cap) → must migrate to B, migration cost at that point.
- If need is uncertain but 300GB plausible: B now avoids later migration, but pays simple-vs-complex maintenance premium.
- Decision hinges on: probability/timing of >100GB, cost of migration later, maintenance cost delta, whether A headroom 80/100 = 80% utilization is acceptable risk buffer.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.
